(frog-nmr-equiv)=
# frog-nmr-equiv

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-info}`NMR` Detect NMR-equivalent atoms from point-group symmetry and topology (methyl rotors).

## What it does

A QM calculation gives one shielding per atom, but in the spectrum chemically equivalent
nuclei (the three H of a methyl group, the two ortho H of a phenyl ring) give one signal. This
command tells you which atoms are equivalent, so you know which computed values to average
and how many signals to expect. `frog-nmr` uses the same detection when it simulates
spectra; run this command to check it or to plan the comparison with experiment.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-nmr-equiv/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

A geometry: an `.xyz` file or an ORCA/Gaussian output (the first structure in the file is
used). It should be optimised: equivalence is found by symmetry, so a distorted geometry hides
symmetric atoms. No NMR calculation is needed.

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` … | required | Geometry file(s) (.xyz, .out, .log) |

**Options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-b`, `--buffer` `BUFFER` | `0.3` | Tolerance added to covalent radii for connectivity in Å |
| `-d`, `--decimals` `DECIMALS` | `4` | Decimals used to compare coordinates |
| `--one-based` |  | Print 1-based atom indices |
| `--include-h-sym` |  | Include H atoms in the point-group detection |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet`, `--format {table,json,csv}`, `--table-file PATH` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terminal | `Equivalencies (<file>)` | always | One row per group of equivalent atoms: element, size, atom indices and a note |

### How to read it

An info line with the point group found on the heavy atoms (H ignored, unless `--include-h-sym`)
and a table with one row per group: element, number of atoms **N**, their indices and a note
(`Rotor / Sym` for groups of ≥ 3 H, `CH2` for any pair of H, `Aromatic / Ring` for ≥ 6 C).

* Examples: methane → Td, one group of 4 H; toluene → C2v (heavy atoms), groups C 0,2 / C 3,5,
  ortho H 7,8, meta H 9,11 and the methyl H 12,13,14.
* The `CH2` note only means "two equivalent H": in toluene it is printed for the ortho and meta
  ring protons, in water for the two OH.
* A C1 molecule gives mostly groups of one atom; freely rotating CH3 (and similar rotors) are still
  merged because they average fast on the NMR time scale.
* Diastereotopic CH2 protons are correctly **not** merged (they are not equivalent).

## Step by step

1. Run `frog-nmr-equiv opt.xyz`; several files can be given at once.
2. Add `--one-based` if you want atom numbers counted from 1, as in most viewers and in `frog-nmr` labels (H24 = index 23).
3. If a group you expect is missing on a slightly distorted geometry, relax the tolerances: `-d 3` compares coordinates with 3 decimals instead of 4; `-b` changes the bond-detection tolerance (Å).

## Full reference

Every option, as printed by `frog-nmr-equiv --help`:

:::{dropdown} `frog-nmr-equiv --help`
```text
usage: frog-nmr-equiv [-h] [-v] [-q] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--table-file PATH] [-b BUFFER]
                      [-d DECIMALS] [--one-based] [--include-h-sym]
                      file [file ...]

Detect NMR-equivalent atoms from point-group symmetry and topology (methyl rotors).

The point group is detected on the heavy atoms (unless --include-h-sym); its operations and the
local graph topology (freely rotating CH3 and similar groups) define the groups of chemically
equivalent nuclei.

positional arguments:
  file                          Geometry file(s) (.xyz, .out, .log)

options:
  -h, --help                    show this help message and exit
  -b BUFFER, --buffer BUFFER    Tolerance added to covalent radii for connectivity in Å (default:
                                0.3)
  -d DECIMALS, --decimals DECIMALS
                                Decimals used to compare coordinates (default: 4)
  --one-based                   Print 1-based atom indices
  --include-h-sym               Include H atoms in the point-group detection

output:
  -v, --verbose                 Enable debug output
  -q, --quiet                   Suppress banner, info and saved-file messages
  --format {table,json,csv}     Format of the tables printed on stdout (default: table)
  --table-file PATH             Also write all tables to PATH (.json, .csv or .txt; otherwise the
                                --format is used)

outputs:
  terminal (stdout; --format table|json|csv, --table-file PATH):
    Equivalencies (<file>)      One row per group of equivalent atoms: element, size, atom indices
                                and a note

examples:
  frog-nmr-equiv opt.xyz
      Equivalent groups with 0-based indices
  frog-nmr-equiv conf_*.out --one-based --format csv
      Several files, 1-based indices, as CSV

Data go to stdout, messages to stderr. Atom indices are 0-based unless stated otherwise.
Step-by-step guide (what it is for, what you need, what to expect): docs/cli/frog-nmr-equiv.md.
```
:::
